inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The prompt says to keep going until every row is complete, with retries and sub-agent spawning, and no bounded stop condition.
The design relies on prompt instructions to manage retries and completeness, with no structural spend, rate, step, or runtime limits described.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Prompt directs retries and completeness checks
controls.decay_rationale: The model is asked to judge completeness and continue retrying; stronger models and longer horizons make it more capable of pursuing the unbounded goal rather than stopping safely.

controls.name: Hard spend cap or monthly call budget on enrichment account
Maximum unattended steps, retries, and runtime
Structural cap on sub-agent spawning depth and count
Spend or quota depletion alert on enrichment account

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries and recursive sub-agent spawning can exhaust the shared enrichment quota

forecast.watch_signal: Median retries or total tool calls per nightly batch rises, or model/version changes, while no structural spend or step limits are added.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to retry failed or incomplete lookups, spawn researcher sub agents, and keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call, and the API key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing so quota exhaustion disrupts other teams.
The nightly batch is 40,000 rows and about 3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result, creating a persistent failure set that can drive repeated retries.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Add a hard spend cap or per-batch call budget on enrich.lookup tied to the shared quota.
Enforce maximum retries, maximum unattended steps, and maximum runtime per account and per batch.
Cap sub-agent spawn depth and total researcher count so recursion cannot multiply paid calls.
Add spend alerts and quota depletion alerts on the enrichment account with automatic batch halt thresholds.

stride_coverage.rationale: No inbound authentication surface, peer protocol, or impersonation path for this standalone batch design is described in the provided artifacts.
The artifacts describe no writable tool definitions, prompt updates, or self-configuration path that would let this agent's process be tampered with.
The artifacts do not say whether agent actions are logged with attributable provenance separate from a generic batch identity.
The described design performs paid lookup and CRM write only; no sensitive outbound data disclosure path outside the trust boundary is evidenced.
No evidence shows the agent gaining broader authority than intended beyond using a shared service account for the paid lookup capability.
The artifacts do not state how the nightly CRM batch source is authenticated or whether source authenticity is verified before processing.
The artifacts do not say whether the source system preserves attributable records for which batch rows were supplied and processed.
No write path to the shared quota store itself is described; the risk here is depletion through legitimate use, not alteration of the store.
The shared quota and API key store is mentioned only as a billing and availability dependency, not as a disclosed data path in this design.
The artifacts do not specify transport integrity, request signing, or other measures protecting outbound lookup calls from alteration in transit.
The artifacts do not state whether outbound lookup requests are encrypted or whether request payloads expose sensitive CRM data beyond company identifiers.

rating.rationale: Manual validation only; scripts could not be run in this environment. Present risk is driven by a property finding: the design has no spend, step, retry, runtime, or sub-agent limits while using a paid shared-quota API across a 40,000-row batch with a known persistent failure subset. Under rubric section 5a, the affected capability set includes S3 spend and delegate actions, with the autonomy modifier applying because the agent is A4 and can spawn agents, yielding inherent high. The only declared control is a prompt-based retry/completeness instruction, which is behavioral and dependent, so residual drops one tier to moderate. Forecast returns to high if longer task horizon, autonomy increase, model upgrade, or control removal defeats that behavioral control. The assessment reflects declared design and configuration artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided by the user, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, tool manifest, or runtime telemetry was provided, so confidence is limited to what the prompt and runtime notes explicitly state.
Authentication, transport protections, logging, and exact sub-agent implementation details were not provided, so several STRIDE pairs are marked not_assessed.
